reviews.text: There's no coordination in giving you attention, and they end up leaving you waiting all day for days until they tell you they don't have appointments for another 3 months.

Excellent place to take your beloved pets to receive medical attention with accurate diagnosis and very good care. Take in consideration they do not have emergency services, only programmed procedures so if your pet is in a life threatening situation here IS NOT the place.

I went to make an appointment, they were very kind, but the surprise was that they accept walk-in dogs in a line. I'll tell you more later; my dog ​​has cancer, and I hope they can give her the care she needs and we can save her!
Everything was excellent, but you do need to allow plenty of time.
They have many phone numbers listed, but none of them answer to schedule an appointment.
My dog ​​is seen by both ethologists and dermatologists, and I'm very grateful for the results of the treatments. They are very professional and provide excellent care for both my dog ​​and me.

Make an appointment, always. The hospital is overcrowded in some specialty areas, and sometimes you have to wait a long time for an appointment, but it's highly recommended. The costs of services and tests are very affordable, almost 50% less than elsewhere.

If you're driving, enter through the faculty parking lot (the one next to Puma Gourmet). It costs $10. Keep in mind that in the afternoon and during class periods, the parking lot fills up, and you have to wait for a car to leave. Even so, after going for over a year, up to four times a month, I've only had to wait twice.

The whole process usually takes between two and four hours, and remember that you only have a 15-minute grace period for your appointment.

If it's your first time, it's a good idea to bring your pet's vaccination record, and if possible, bring your pet's medical history, including any illnesses, etc.

Also, if you're going for a second opinion or because you want to change doctors, it's a good idea to bring their previous test results and prescriptions. Unlike other hospitals (I'm talking to you, Banfield), if the tests are recent, they'll accept them from other institutions and won't make you repeat them.

The vets take a very detailed medical history. They're also open on Saturdays, although their services are very limited. They accept card and cash payments. If you want to buy water or coffee, there's a stand right under the stairs in the hospital building.

If you don't have an appointment, you have to wait quite a while; I went on Saturday and waited a little over an hour and a half. But if they do see you, they're kind to you and your pet. The only downside is that they told me they didn't offer imaging studies on weekends due to administrative reasons, and in the end, they referred me to another hospital, but they didn't charge me anything.

The service was good and somewhat quick; however, I brought my dog's previous tests, and they still performed the same tests there, claiming it was necessary because the originals weren't clear. I brought digital copies, and they were perfectly clear. In the end, they gave me the diagnosis I already knew and refused to schedule surgery because the hospital's schedule was full. So why even see you if they're not going to do anything? They charged me 2,000 pesos for something I already knew and had brought.

I absolutely do not recommend this hospital. They just take your money and then leave you hanging, not caring at all. Seriously, don't go there!

I've read several reviews, and they mention the cost, the quality of service, and the doctors' treatment.

I'd like to share our experience. We took Canelo there, initially for a skin condition and later for lymphoma.
Our experience has been entirely positive.
Regarding the cost, it's not free; the checkup costs $250. If tests are required, they also cost money, at a moderate price.
Regarding the service, I want to express my gratitude to all the doctors, students, and staff. While we've been seen by a different doctor almost every time we've gone, the treatment has always been incredibly empathetic, sensitive, supportive, and humane.

Finally, I want to mention that if it's not critical, try to make an appointment by phone; it takes some time, but it's possible. If it's more urgent, then arrive before 10:00 a.m. They always have openings. You'll have to wait a few hours, but it's completely worth it.
I highly recommend it. If it's your first time, arrive early and be patient; it's very busy, but the service is top-notch.
Excellent service
I took Junior to the doctor because he was having seizures. Thanks to these kids and their teachers, Junior is under control and the seizures have decreased.
Good hospital, good service, accurate diagnoses, affordable cost. You can tell they're studying because they love what they do.
Excellent service and everyone was very friendly
Hello, I tried to contact you to make an appointment but the number is disconnected.
They took very good care of my lovebird

The residents and doctors treat you with excellent care, very humanely. They explain things very patiently and treat the animals much better than some private hospitals that prioritize profit. It can take time, but it's worth it.
Excellent hospital. One of the best!
We received excellent service!
Excellent and quick service in the emergency room! Thank you for saving my dog!

Great place, lots of specialists, excellent check-up and care even in the emergency room. Buuuut... if you're looking for speed or think that because you're paying, they're at your service, forget it, don't waste your time. Their priority is your pet, appointments take a while, and at most, they'll wait a couple of hours, if not half a day, so be patient.
Excellent treatment, attention and care from all the doctors.
The medical staff is excellent and very well prepared.
There are only appointments available in the Cardiology specialty until November 2026; today is July 27th.

Without a doubt, it's a place full of professionals who love their work, always concerned about your pet's well-being, and ensuring that you, as the owner, understand what they're telling you.
It's a bit pricey, but that's not the veterinarians' fault. I will definitely return.
Very good service
Good service, a bit pricey

I took my dog ​​to the vet because she had bruising and low platelets. Before that, I had taken her to about five veterinarians, and they all said her tick bite lab results were negative, so it was probably an autoimmune disease, which gave a poor prognosis. They said she needed a platelet transfusion just to buy time to diagnose the cause of the low platelets, which was very expensive. I decided to take her to the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) because no one else was treating her. There, they did a PCR test, and it came back positive for herlichiosis. They immediately started treatment, and my dog ​​recovered. I am very grateful to the doctors; they provided excellent care and service. You have to pay for the tests, but they are cheaper than at any other clinic or external veterinary lab.
They are very attentive, friendly, and explain things very well.

The best place in Mexico City to get your dog and cat treated! Very professional and fair prices. They offer all specialties and emergency services. Although they're only open Monday through Saturday,
Excellent service

Excellent service with 80% satisfaction.
The only thing they don't have is an MRI.
Otherwise, the service is excellent overall.
Affordable prices.
It might be a little slow, but the service is good.
They never answer the phones, therefore I cannot make an appointment.
Excellent care and excellent veterinary medical service
Excellent care and service at affordable prices, very humane for the care of your pets

This is my first time here and I thought the service was excellent. Everyone was very attentive and clearly enjoys their work. I need to go back for a follow-up appointment for my dog, and I will.
Thank you 🙏💕 …

Excellent oncology care. My dog ​​arrived with lymphoma and difficulty breathing. He was seen immediately and started chemotherapy that same week. Today, almost a year later, he has a good quality of life and continues treatment.

They also saved his life from a brown recluse spider bite. It's expensive, but totally worth it. A great specialty hospital.
They are not answering on any of their three numbers to schedule an appointment, I have been calling since 10:00 am, it is 11:45 am and nothing.

It's an excellent hospital. Note! Don't confuse it with the UNAM Banfield Veterinary Hospital; that's a different one.
At this one, the UNAM Veterinary Specialty Hospital, I took my dog ​​Zeus to neurology, and I was surprised by the excellent care. It's immediately clear they are highly trained. My dog ​​has had an excellent recovery. I still need to get an MRI, which they don't perform here. But my experience was the best. They were very kind, treated my dog ​​very well, and above all, they are very good veterinarians. Thank you!

If you love your pet, please don't go here. We went here hoping to get a second opinion on my dog's hip pain. He arrived walking, they gave him medication, and the pain progressed to him being unable to walk at all. They scheduled appointments every three days, and it was just more and more money and more expensive tests. My brother spent a fortune hoping he would walk again. The dog deteriorated, and in the end, their supposed diagnosis was cancer. They wanted to extract blood from his bone marrow, and that's when we suspected they were using him as a guinea pig. At that point, we went to another veterinarian, but it was too late. The dog started suffering from kidney failure, and they told us it was due to the medications they gave him at this so-called hospital. We couldn't do anything, and my dog ​​died last week. We had to put him to sleep because he was suffering too much from the medications they gave him here. My mother and brother are devastated by the loss of my dog. We are going to pursue legal action for medical negligence.

Truly the best place to bring your pets!
Yes, it's a teaching hospital, so students or interns will attend to your pet, but they're always supervised by a specialist!
They're very empathetic. The waits are often long, but they'll talk to you and explain the situation. If, for some reason, they can't see your pet, they'll give you recommendations.
Their prices are affordable. They have the same vacation schedule as the UNAM Administrative Faculty. They treat dogs and cats in the main building, but other specialties are also available in a separate building. Honestly, of all the places I've been to, this has been the best, with the best doctors.
I'm sure Lina received the best treatment, and everyone fought alongside her. Everything was done so she could live as well as possible, without pain.
Thank you for everything.
There are never any appointments available, and if there are, they schedule them 4 or 5 months later. Their telephone service is terrible.
The diagnostic service is excellent, but the prices are a bit high.

Unfortunately, the system is like the IMSS (Mexican Social Security Institute): there are no appointments available for three months, and to get seen you have to go early and stand in line to see if they'll see you.
Great place, highly recommended, easy to get to and cheap
They are very attentive, although they take a while to deliver test results, so it may be necessary to ask if you can get them done externally, in order to move forward with an accurate diagnosis.

They only stole about 3,000 pesos from my parents for studies and things like that that they never received; it was practically like wasting a whole day with the dog with its broken leg and throwing that money away

It's expensive, and even if you have an emergency, you still have to make an appointment. If you have another pet present, the initial deposit is 500, and for any emergency needs, it's nearby. But taking kittens is more stressful because the veterinary clinic is almost exclusively for dogs.
Affordable prices and good service from veterinarians
Good

It's a great option for saving money, especially when you're getting several tests done on your pet. So far, all the doctors I've encountered have been incredibly kind. Not all the administrative staff are as friendly, but they do respond. They offer everything from blood tests and X-rays to consultations. The only downside I see is that the cashiers and some of the testing areas are a bit spread out. And yes, it does take some time between waiting, paying, and the whole process.

They don't answer phone calls, but you can bring your pets without an appointment. The wait is a bit long, but they will see you. The doctors are very kind and professional; I highly recommend them 10/10.

In my case, I took my kitten on a Saturday (without an appointment). They examined her (it was free) and scheduled an appointment that same day with the oncology specialist (for the following Friday). During the specialist appointment, they performed three tests (the consultation with the specialist costs $500, and each test is an additional cost). After the results were in, they scheduled a surgery date. Everything went perfectly, and she is now recovering.
Fast
Due to high workload, they cannot accept your dog without a prior appointment, which takes months, unless the dog is very seriously ill.

I didn't expect them to be so kind. I feel very confident in the diagnosis. The prices are very reasonable.
They are very patient, and you have to be patient too because the wait is long. I would do it again.

Terrible service in the emergency room, don't waste your time.

Bad treatment; the vet was very arrogant. They told me my dog ​​was fine when he wasn't. I waited a long time only to be denied a diagnosis, and they never gave me a prescription.

I decided to leave and take my dog ​​to another vet who told me he was dehydrated and gave me a diagnosis.

👍🏼 The staff is very attentive. They offer a wide variety of specialized services for different species, although most of their patients are dogs and cats.

You can park at the university for only $10 for free parking.

👎🏼 It's almost a miracle to get them to answer the phone. I've spent weeks calling at different times without getting a response. Appointments are scarce, but ironically, they ask you to cancel your phone call if you can't attend.


🚩 Sometimes you're prescribed controlled human medication, and it becomes a nightmare because the prescriptions aren't filled correctly, and pharmacies don't fill them, forcing you to go back again and again. Or worse, they tell you to go to a certain veterinary clinic in Tecamachalco for a prescription for X medication, and when you get there, they see the instructions from HVZ UNAM and say, "Yes, of course, with pleasure. It's $500 for issuing the prescription."

I recommend bringing water and treats for your pet, and always keeping them on a leash and using bags to pick up their waste.

Excellent care from the veterinarians.

They explained in detail the procedures my pet would require and offered me several food options to suit my budget.

Although the service can be slow due to high demand, they give you peace of mind knowing your pet is in good hands.
The doctors are very good, the waiting time can sometimes be a bit long, but the specialties they have help a lot with the diagnoses of the furry ones and also kittens.

We took a rescued puppy with trauma and eye problems, an appointment was made and even confirmed, and at the last minute it turns out that she wasn't there, they didn't even put down the details or write down the corresponding names, on top of that now we have to wait more than 2 months for them to take place.
Excellent service, they were very patient in explaining everything. It was a bit slow, but they treated my puppy very well.

It's closed for the entire holiday period. Are you a hospital? Don't you know that diseases don't care about holidays? They say to come back on January 5th, but my dog ​​won't be back by then. At least update your hours.
Hi! Does anyone know how I can make an appointment by phone? The number listed here isn't working 🥲. If anyone knows, I'd really appreciate it!! …
They are excellent. I've had my 18-year-old dog treated there in cardiology and my female dog in orthopedics with wonderful results and care.
They treated my kitten very well. Thank you so much for checking him over thoroughly.
Excellent service and attention. All the staff are very friendly. They accept walk-ins, but it's subject to staff availability. They accept card payments 💳. …
Excellent service and prices, plus the place is super quiet for dogs, none of them get stressed since it's outdoors in a very spacious area

The challenge if you arrive after 10:00 AM is finding parking.

The service at the hospital is excellent. They treat pets incredibly well.
Excellent service and great treatment for pets.

The staff is very friendly, there is one line for people with appointments and one without appointments, unfortunately if you are looking for ultrasounds or anything related to radiology they do not attend to you without appointments and these can take up to more than two months.

I've been taking my dog ​​there for two months now. At first, like anywhere, the wait can be a little long, but because of the diagnosis, which was an emergency, he was seen the same day I brought him in, and the same day I left, his next appointments were already scheduled. The treatment we've received has been excellent, humane, and the doctors are very committed. It's a teaching hospital, and I think many people should understand that. It doesn't mean the staff isn't professional or well-prepared; it means there are many student doctors at different levels, but they're always supervised by attending physicians. It's been two months now, and I've noticed a remarkable improvement in Kimbo. His quality of life has improved. He's currently undergoing chemotherapy, and I'm very grateful for the services the hospital provides, which are also very affordable. A major strength of the hospital is that it has different specialties in one place, and the consultations are very convenient. Here are some photos from his first chemo session :D
Very professional, super friendly, super attentive, and very careful! My kitten is extremely small, and yet they did everything they could to take care of him.
Excellent place and fair prices

Horrible and expensive. I took my pet for a dental cleaning and they wanted to neuter him. The services are extremely expensive, and it's a lie that they offer discounts from UNAM (National Autonomous University of Mexico). I recommend the vet who treats my pets; he charges 100 pesos per consultation and is very professional and good at his treatments. If you truly love your pets, don't take them there. It's pure business and a way to rip you off; they only profit from the love we have for our pets. I recommend you look for the UNAM Veterinary Specialty Postgraduate Hospital. Just past that little hospital, enter the faculty area against the flow of traffic on the avenue, and it's about 20 steps in front of the Postgraduate Dentistry building. They give appointments at 11 am. There are usually a lot of people, but it's worth it; they're postgraduate and they give thorough checkups. 💕🐱🐶 Check their website and you'll see they have most specialties except dental and no prophylaxis. For those who like this, I recommend a fantastic doctor near Plaza Tepeyac. He charges a fair price, or even more, he's very good and has a true vocation for animal welfare; he's saved many.
They are somewhat distracted when assigning appointments, however there are some great and very good veterinarians.
They have all the numbers listed, and none of them answer.
Worse than social security, if you love your pets don't take them there.
Excellent treatment of the animals, they are very humane, they take great care of them, they have everything there at the hospital
Very good service
Poor service, negligence, it's the IMSS for dogs... the IMSS in times of neoliberalism

Is there a phone number where someone actually answers to schedule an appointment?
I've been trying to get through for two days at all hours.
Thanks
Excellent care, equipment, facilities, and doctors
I find the medication prescribed for my puppy

The care is excellent, especially since they have several specialties. The costs are low compared to some other specialty hospitals. Overall, I'm very grateful to the doctors; they are very kind, attentive, and loving with our pets.

My dog ​​with skin cancer had been to several places; they were going to operate and remove his penis to take off the growths, but that didn't solve the problem. Fortunately, I came here where they performed a much gentler operation because they told me the one they were suggesting could make him even worse. I'm grateful for the care and the better solution. We're still undergoing treatment, but this is the best place I've found so far.
The information on their website is not up to date, and as other users have mentioned, they accept walk-ins from 10 am, but it's best to arrive 15 or 20 minutes early.

I've tried contacting them to schedule an appointment, but they never answer, on any of their numbers. If anyone could, or has a number where they can provide information and schedule an appointment, I would be very grateful.

I took my adopted Chihuahua from Acapulco to receive treatment for heartworms. I was desperate; I had already taken him to several veterinary hospitals, where they all insisted on heart surgery to remove the worms one by one. I refused because Totopo is an 11-year-old dog, very small, and I knew he wouldn't survive the surgery. Everywhere I went, they gave him a terminal diagnosis if I didn't have the surgery (which was very expensive, by the way). Finally, a doctor recommended you. Thank God I followed her advice, made an appointment, and took Totopo for a consultation. Besides being incredibly professional, offering all kinds of tests at a very affordable price, you also offered a treatment to eliminate the worms without surgery. It was a medication protocol combined with injections, and there was no need for an operation.

Totopo followed the entire treatment plan and is now heartworm-free. Words cannot express my gratitude for saving my dog's life. Thank you to all the doctors in the cardiology department. Thanks to you, Totopo will live many more years with me. I highly recommend them. They provide excellent care, follow-up care, are very professional, and the price is very reasonable. Without a doubt, the best experience, and they truly care about your pet.

Totopo and I will always be very grateful!
Hello, good evening. I have a question. Could you please give me a number to schedule an appointment?
Are they working?
They have specialized services for pets and good service.

They brought my life companion back to me.
My dog ​​suddenly collapsed. At first, I took her to a private vet, and her first night alone cost me $10,000, with no improvement whatsoever. They didn't even know what was wrong. I heard about this hospital in Ciudad Universitaria (C.U.), went there, and the change in my dog ​​was remarkable. They saved her life, and I will always be grateful. The costs are affordable, and the staff is incredibly kind. I should mention that during my visits, I noticed they also took in some government rescue dogs from natural disasters. I saw horses, birds, dogs, and cats—your pets will be in good hands. 10000/10

The care is excellent. Although it's a teaching hospital, all the doctors are board-certified, and patient diagnoses and treatments are discussed by a team of physicians. Yes, they perform multiple tests to provide an accurate diagnosis.

In my cat's case, the care and follow-up have been excellent from every medical team that has treated him. They maintain very strict control over each patient through their medical record.

I consider the prices fair; it's not the cheapest place in the world, but they aren't exorbitant either. They don't perform any procedures or tests without the pet owner's prior consent.

There's a 24/7 emergency service if the pet has an open file at the hospital. They only close during vacation periods.

For first-time appointments, you can call to schedule or go directly to the hospital. They start seeing patients at 10:00 AM. It's very important to keep in mind that the wait is long, but it's definitely worth it.
The students of the FMVZ of the UNAM take great care of the animals that arrive there.
Excellent care from specialists

Excellent care. I took my dog ​​in for a cruciate ligament rupture. All the doctors who treated her, from the first visit, during and after her surgery, were excellent, very patient and kind. They explained all the procedures very well. The prices are affordable. It's a little difficult to get through on the phone, but other than that, we are very happy and grateful to the specialists in the orthopedics area, the surgeons, and the anesthesiology department.
Excellent
Excellent service, they were very kind to our little Tobby!!!
Very bad experience. They don't take care of the animals.
The doctors will attend to and follow up on your case.

Very friendly, a little slow but that's due to the number of patients.
Very good and affordable service.

The care my pet has received has ranged from fair to good, sometimes with accurate diagnosis and treatment, and other times not so much. But what is truly annoying is the excessive wait time for appointments at the IMSS (Mexican Social Security Institute) pet clinic. Why give you an appointment time if they don't see you until an hour and a half later? You literally lose half a day or more there, and on top of that, they don't answer calls until 5:00 PM. They really have a lot of room for improvement. They're like the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM). 😒

Terrible service. They barely examined my dog. The supposed veterinarian didn't even look at the tests I brought, and he told me it would take hours to find an opening to see her. I told him I would wait, and after five minutes he came out to tell me that he had an operating room available that day, that my dog ​​urgently needed surgery, and he took me to a hallway to give me a list of hospitals. It seems like it's all about making money. The doctor is awful; he has no compassion whatsoever, and it's a teaching hospital. I don't even want to imagine how the students this doctor is in charge of turn out.
Excellent service, good explanation, reasonable waiting time
The best service

I took my dog ​​there who had a transmissible venereal tumor, and the doctors provided excellent care. They were always attentive and friendly to their patients, and it's much more affordable than other private vets, from what I heard. In the end, my dog ​​made a full recovery ♥️ I highly recommend it
They should only allow one companion in the cat area because it is very small, and up to 3 people per cat.

I take my dog ​​(a 9-year-old pit bull) there for skin and joint problems. I've been very pleased with the care they give the dogs, although appointments can take a while depending on the specialty. The prices are reasonable compared to other specialty hospitals. However, it is slow due to high demand.

I don't recommend taking your pets for anything more specialized; maybe just the diagnosis and that's it. But look for many more options because if you leave them there, it will end up costing more than it's worth, and it won't be completely resolved. At least that's what happened in our case.
We paid $13,000 and change in total just for an enema for my kitten, 5 days of hospitalization (I was surprised they couldn't discharge him, and on top of that, he got an infection :c), and lab tests.
After that, we took him to some veterinarians who specialize in cats, and they scolded us because they bluntly told us that it costs a lot of money there, they drag things out, and on top of that, they're all just trainees. Just be very careful.
I really hope you don't have the bad experience I had.
Very good care, excellent service from all the doctors
Excellent service
They open at 10am. They provide good service and treat your pet well.
DO NOT TAKE YOUR PETS. Their procedures are inadequate and the specialists are terrible; there are many deaths they cannot explain.

They provide excellent care for animals; the veterinarians are licensed and completing their specialization, and they are advised and guided by specialists. So far, I've been pleased with how they treat my pet.
Excellent service. Affordable prices.

I went to the clinic in early March of 2025 to ask for information about taking my kitten to a vet. I told them I had already taken him to two private veterinarians, and they said he needed to see an ophthalmologist. Since I didn't have an appointment, they told me to arrive early, at ten in the morning, so they could assess my kitten and see him. Eight days later, I went very early, traveling from a great distance, hoping my kitten would finally be seen. When I arrived, they told me he needed to see a specialist, but that they couldn't do it at that moment because they were fully booked. They just gave me a list of private hospitals to take him to. How could they be so inhuman? My kitten urgently needed medical attention, and they refused to see him. My kitten was very nervous, and it was difficult to transport him there because I was worried his condition would worsen. In desperation, I asked several people there for help, but they refused. They ignored my request and even said they didn't have an emergency room, even though I had gone there eight days earlier to ask for information and was told they would see him. They just deceived me. What a disappointment! I thought that because it's the most prestigious university, they would give my kitten the care he needed, but they didn't.
Excellent service and the best veterinary care, very professional, excellent and not too expensive

Inexperienced students with an arrogant attitude. It's like a public hospital.

Since it's a student hospital, about five 'doctors' go into the examination room, but they don't let you in because of 'Covid protocol.' This was last year, 2024.

They performed tests on her, but they didn't have the courtesy to tell me what procedures they would do (for example, injecting her bladder). They must have treated her very badly because at the next appointment they told me she wouldn't let them handle her and they couldn't do the remaining tests. They prescribed a sedative for the next appointment and told me they wouldn't see her if she didn't arrive sedated.

The worst part is that, because there's a long wait between appointments, different students see you each time; even the person in charge isn't the same. This results in contradictions regarding the treatment...

My cat has asthma. At the first appointment, they prescribed a temporary medication. The next time, they continued with that medication and increased the dosage. In subsequent appointments (justifying it by saying I'd taken too long to get the kitten used to the inhaler for asthma), they told me we'd have to continue using the medication, which, according to the first veterinarian, would be temporary. I was saddened to learn that this medication can't be given for more than three months because it can cause kidney, liver, and hormonal damage.

I don't know who supervises these kids. I understand they offer 'affordable' prices in exchange for students 'practicing and learning' on your pet, but they could certainly benefit from some thorough audits.
Very good service, but if you go without an appointment you'll be there all day.

Don't take your animals there; they really just waste your time and money, and in the end, they don't give you a diagnosis or answer your calls. There's no follow-up, and the staff is very disorganized. I hope these people never work on the street or open a business because they claim to be students, but they don't know anything at all.

Their service is absolutely terrible. I took my dog ​​there without an appointment, and they took all day. This place was recommended to me, but honestly, it's not worth it. They ran tests on my dog, supposedly as an emergency, but they didn't give me the results that same day. They called me later and told me she needed more tests. I had them done because of the love you have for your pets and because you want them to be well. The next day, I went back to get them done, but I wasted the whole day again. They told me they would send the results by mail, but I still haven't received anything. They don't answer the phone; they tell me to call back tomorrow or that they'll contact me so the doctor can tell me what to do next. In total, I spent 7,000 pesos on tests, and to this day, my dog ​​still doesn't have any medication or treatment. I really don't know why people take their pets there. It's not cheap, and they're not honest.

I have no words to express my gratitude for the care they give their patients.
Regarding my dog, they were always attentive and understanding. They explained everything in detail, especially since the hospital operates as a teaching hospital. When you bring your dog in, they explain the suspected diagnosis, the diagnostic process, the treatment, and the prognosis.

The high-quality, specialized care they provide is not reflected in the price.

Keep in mind that, being a high-demand hospital, you need to dedicate a significant amount of time (they tell you this from the beginning).
Parking is limited.
If it's your first time visiting: bring lunch, water, and food and water for your pets.
They accept card payments.

As always, excellent service from top professionals. I'm so proud of all the students and academics who work there; they're among the best in Mexico. I took my dog ​​in for a tumor, and they operated on it. Now she's cured thanks to their care.
Terrible service. I've been calling daily for over 15 days to try to make an appointment and no one answers. How is it possible that out of 3 lousy numbers, they can't answer any of them?

Excellent. My pet received excellent care. Unfortunately, the service is limited. It took me three months to get an appointment. It's not a suitable place for emergencies. If you need a specialist, it's better to go to the UVM Hospital; obviously, it's more expensive, but the care is more immediate.
Punctual and friendly veterinarians. Without a doubt, the best veterinary hospital in Mexico City.
The service is top-notch; appointments are recommended, but if your pet needs emergency care, they'll see you very quickly. The doctors are excellent.
Good service
The doctor who treated Cuchu was very kind and explained the diagnosis and treatment plan in detail. This is the second time we've been to the hospital. A good veterinary hospital.
A very good place, they take the time to explain everything about your pet's diagnosis and provide excellent service. Highly recommended.
Excellent service!
Excellent attention, patience and service

I appreciate the attention and service. The staff is professional and knowledgeable. We are very happy with the care our dog Henry has received at the Veterinary Hospital of our university, UNAM! Thank you for everything you do for the animals!

The worst place, the guardians look like they're made of money, and the treatment is very classist from the so-called "residents". No graduate veterinarian will attend to your dogs, cats, or whatever you bring in, look for other options.

As it's a teaching hospital, the veterinarians there have limited experience, and they rotate every two weeks, which means patient information gets lost with each doctor. They are advised by more experienced veterinarians, but with so many cases, they don't give each one the attention it deserves. They keep a record, but as the weeks go by, your pet's information gets lost. I took my cat there for several months, and they never gave me a definitive diagnosis. I paid a lot of money, ran out of money, and in the end, I still had to put my pet down because he deteriorated. Perhaps it's okay to take them for simpler diagnoses, but I wouldn't recommend it for complex problems. I'm just sharing my experience.
